- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for negative sentiment.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment, leading to overshoots in 30-day forecasts; apply smoothing or decay factor to recent spikes.
- Mean reversion is evident: forecasts often drift away from recent 18-day average; adjust toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently fails to capture long-term trend shifts; use sentiment momentum (last 3–5 sentiment values) to adjust for trend persistence.
- If sentiment shows sudden reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), reduce forecast magnitude by 15–30% to account for volatility shift.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment-driven spikes beyond 5–7 days; cap forecast growth after sentiment peaks to prevent runaway inflation.
